items.pra-ai-guidance::model-identification: Every model used in prudential decision-making must sit in a firm-wide, documented model inventory, including models built with AI or machine-learning techniques, in-house or third-party. A consistent risk-based tiering by materiality and complexity should determine how much validation effort and control each model receives, so that the most impactful models — including recommendation systems and other qualitative-output AI — get proportionate treatment.
items.pra-ai-guidance::board-governance: The board of directors is accountable for a firm-wide model risk management framework proportionate to the firm's size and model use, sets its model risk appetite, and ensures roles across business, risk, and control functions are defined. Responsibility for the framework must be allocated to the relevant Senior Managers Framework accountability holders, with internal audit providing independent assurance. The same governance expectations apply to externally developed and vendor-supplied models used for prudentially relevant purposes.
items.pra-ai-guidance::development-documentati: Model development, implementation, and use must be documented end to end: defined purpose and design, data quality requirements covering both traditional and alternative data, conceptual soundness review, implementation and change controls, and recorded, justified rationale for any model adjustment or expert-judgement override of model output. Testing should demonstrate the model behaves as intended before use and when its data, design, or assumptions change.
items.pra-ai-guidance::independent-validation: Models require independent validation separate from their development and ownership — conceptual review, ongoing performance monitoring against defined thresholds, and outcome analysis — proportionate to the model's assigned tier. Because model risk rises with complexity that is difficult to understand or explain in non-technical terms, firms applying AI and machine-learning techniques should give weight in tiering and monitoring to interpretability, explainability, transparency, and the potential for designer or data bias, with periodic revalidation.
items.pra-ai-guidance::risk-mitigants: Firms should have established policies for mitigating residual model risk when models under-perform: documented post-model adjustments subject to independent review, clear rules on when a model's use may be restricted, and defined exceptions and escalation routes. Extrapolating beyond a model's operating boundaries — stressed economic conditions, for instance — and reliance on models that are difficult to understand or explain increase model risk and call for stronger mitigants.
